title: Phasebound KPI Anchor & Traffic Containment Plan
content:
Purpose:
This doc defines a compact, phasebound KPI anchoring approach and a lightweight traffic containment plan for new feature rollouts (canary -> ramp -> scale). It is intentionally operational: short checklist, thresholds, owners, comms templates, and a mini-sim script for running a 60-minute surge drill. Use this as the single-source operational play for small-to-medium feature launches where Dedicated capacity and Hosted API routing intersect.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: feature launches that touch inference routes (generation/embed/rerank) and could change per-token cost or latency distribution.
- Audience: product-ops, SRE, serving-runtime oncall, solutions-eng, release lead.

High-level philosophy (one-liner):
Anchor decisions to 3 live KPIs + one safety signal (errors) and predefine containment steps for each phase.

Phase definitions (how we use "phasebound"):
- Canary: 0.5%–2% traffic, initial 24–72h. Tight SLOs, manual guardrail checks.
- Ramp: 2%–20% traffic, rolling increments, automated gating allowed.
- Scale: >20% traffic, full monitoring and auto-rollbacks enabled.

Core KPIs (measurement cadence and owners):
- p50/p95 latency (ms) — owner: serving-runtime (Marcus Patel) — cadence: 5m
- Cost per 1k tokens (USD) — owner: product-ops finance lead (Sofia Alvarez) — cadence: daily and estimated realtime cost by routing bucket
- Model quality delta (eval set score, e.g., rouge/f1/embedding-sim) — owner: applied-ml (Ethan Brooks) — cadence: after each model variant push / hourly for smoke evals
- Safety signal: error rate (5xx + throttles) — owner: SRE (Priya Nambiar) — cadence: 1m

Threshold guide (examples — adapt per-feature):
- Canary pass condition -> p95 latency increase < 20% relative to baseline AND error rate < 0.5% AND quality delta within tolerance (-1.0% absolute relative to baseline).
- Ramp gate -> p95 < 30% increase, error rate < 1.0%, cost delta < 35% (unless commercial-approved).
- Scale acceptance -> sustained metrics within ramp gates for 48h and cost runway validated.

Mini KPI table (copy/paste into sheet as baseline):
| KPI | baseline | canary-threshold | ramp-threshold | owner | measure-freq |
| p50 latency (ms) | 120 | +15% | +25% | Marcus | 5m |
| p95 latency (ms) | 520 | +20% | +30% | Marcus | 5m |
| error rate (%) | 0.12 | <0.5 | <1.0 | Priya | 1m |
| cost /1k tokens (USD) | 0.095 | <0.13 | <0.18 | Sofia | daily/realtime |
| eval delta (score) | 0.00 (baseline) | > -1.0% | > -1.5% | Ethan | hourly |

Traffic containment playbook (ordered):
1) Fast-stop (immediate) — Executed by serving-runtime oncall: flip canary routing to baseline variant (traffic switch), stop new deployments. Slack: #prodops-commander -> use template "FAST-STOP: {feature} {time} {reason}".
2) Reduce traffic to safe-slice — adjust rollout weight to 0.1% for 10 minutes, observe signals.
3) Engage owners — auto-page if error rate exceeds page threshold (configured in Opsgenie). Document initial hypothesis in one-line form in incident doc.
4) If mitigation fails, rollback model or route to previous model variant; inform Customer Success if external customers affected.
5) Postmortem capture (24–72h) with signal graphs and root-cause hypothesis; product-ops owns timeline.

Communications templates (short):
- Slack to #prodops-commander: "FAST-STOP: {feature-name} @ {HH:MM UTC}. Triggers: p95 +40% and error-rate 1.8%. Action: routing -> baseline variant, stopping deploys. Owner: {owner}."
- Email to stakeholders: subject "Feature {feature} Canary Halted — Immediate Notice" body with 3 bullets: what, observed, immediate action.

Surge drill (60-minute runbook for tabletop + live smoke):
- T-30m: align owners, confirm baseline metrics, enable extended retention for metrics (to capture minute-level).
- T-10m: inject traffic pattern in staging matching 3x expected concurrency for 10 minutes. Observe latency/error/cost signals.
- T+0: start canary at 2% with synthetic load for 15 minutes. If p95 latency > canary-threshold -> execute Fast-stop.
- T+30m: review logs, confirm if routing rollback was clean. Capture cost delta.
- T+60m: decision: continue to ramp or abort. Capture decision and rationale into Confluence stub noted in linked_artifacts.

Quick rollout checklist (pre-launch):
- [ ] Baseline metrics snapshot (last 7d, owner: Marcus)
- [ ] Cost-runway estimate for projected qps (owner: Sofia)
- [ ] Eval suite smoke (owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Canary routing plan + oncall hours roster (owner: product-ops release lead)
- [ ] Comm templates prefilled and Slack channel reserved (owner: product-ops)
- [ ] Feature flag + kill-switch tested end-to-end (engineering)
- [ ] Legal/compliance signoff if model handles customer PII (security/compliance)

Open questions / unresolved decisions (notes to self):
- Do we allow automated ramp beyond 10% for Hosted customers? (Need pricing approval if cost delta > 20%)
- Consider adding a 'quality-safety' metric that blends eval delta with user-reported regressions; prototype with 3 test prompts.

Post-launch capture (first-48h requirements):
- Product-ops: daily standup for first 3 days of rollout (15m) capturing any metric drift.
- SRE: create a short incident board if error spikes >2x baseline. Include link to live traces.
- Applied-ML: hourly quality smoke for first 24h after each model push.

Appendix: quick links & artifacts
- Confluence spec: PRODOPS-5234-phasebound-kpi-spec (see linked_artifacts)
- Canary routing runbook (internal doc -> /internal/infra/canary-routing)
- Template: postmortem checklist (use standard ops template)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is deliberately concise and ops-oriented. If you think a KPI is missing for your area (e.g., token-variance or cache-hit-rate), add under "kpi table" and call out the owner.
- Proposed next steps after approval: (1) replicate the KPI table into product-ops shared sheet with formulas for percent-delta and alert flags; (2) add Opsgenie escalation policy tied to these thresholds; (3) schedule a 60-minute surge drill with SRE and serving-runtime.

Authorship & history:
- Drafted by: Ava Chen (product-ops).
- Reviewed: Marcus Patel (serving-runtime), Sofia Alvarez (finance), Ethan Brooks (applied-ml), Priya Nambiar (sre).
- Last updated: 2024-09-04 — clarified ramp thresholds and added surge-drill script.
